goal: Each kind of area has its own root under `~/mc`: `plan/<programme>/` (unchanged), `step/<project>/` for the runner's areas, `work/<name>/` for `mc work`. What an area is follows from its path. There is no marker file, and no lookup in the register decides it.

A finished project leaves a closeout in git, `docs/project/<programme>/closeout/<project>.json`, written in the same archive PR that removes its plan. It holds the goal, the steps with PR, sha and date, and time, tokens and cost per session. After that, mc removes the project's local data: register file, session logs, `runner/log/closed/<project>`, scratch and transcripts.

`mc tidy` applies the retention rules per root. The runner runs it once a day, and again when lanes are skipping for low disk. A programme keeps its current conversation, and the others go after 72 h. A planning area keeps its two checkouts, and extra worktrees go once they are finished. A work area stays until `mc work release`/`discard`. Before deleting, `mc tidy` writes the list of what it will delete to a file, and it deletes only from that list.
contract: A programme is long-lived and a project is not (ruling 39). A project's data is never pruned by age while the project is open, even when a step waits a week on a timed blocker (`releaseDue`, ruling 35). It goes only after the project's closeout is on `origin/main` and its area is gone.

A planning area's `memoro/` and `memoro-cli/` checkouts are never removed by tidy, however long the programme has been idle. Extra worktrees in a planning area are allowed, for example a subagent's. Tidy removes one only when `releaseVerdict` (`src/mc/work-area.js`) says worktree and branch can go: clean, nothing main lacks, and no process standing in it.
A work area (`~/mc/work/<name>/`) is never removed by tidy or the runner, only by `mc work release` or `mc work discard`. Its transcripts go with it, as they do today.

Nothing in this project deletes a worktree with uncommitted changes or commits main lacks, a `memory/` directory under `~/.claude/projects`, `runs.tsv`, `~/.memoro/mc/gate-rounds.jsonl`, `project_log.md`, or anything outside these roots: `~/mc/step`, `~/mc/work`, `~/mc/plan/<programme>/<extra worktree>`, `~/mc/runner/log`, `~/mc/runner/scratch`, `~/mc/runner/projects`, `~/.claude/projects`. Every removal asserts its path is under one of them (`realpath`) before it touches it.

Every deletion is list-first (ruling 39, after the 2026-09-26 incident in which a failing test inside a shell delete loop removed 190 transcript directories). The list is written whole to a file, and the apply deletes only entries from it. Each entry is re-checked at removal. A check that errors or cannot answer means keep, never delete. Deletion goes through node `fs`, with no shell, no `find`/`bfs` and no globbing.

A project's register file is removed only when all of these hold: its row is in `project_log.md` on `origin/main`, its plan directory is absent on `origin/main`, its closeout file is present on `origin/main`, and no area for it exists. `overlayPlans` (`src/mc/register.js`) re-seeds a missing entry from a plan still on main, so deleting earlier would run the steps again.

Existing areas are not moved. Runner areas at `~/mc/<project>/` keep working, are closed in place, and drain away. New ones are made under `~/mc/step/`. No `git worktree move` is ever run, because transcripts, dev-server records and `current-*.json` hold absolute paths.
Every step runs `npm test` and lands through `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.
out_of_scope: `~/mc/gate`, `~/mc/gate-cache`, `~/.memoro/mc/deploy`, `~/.memoro/mc/managed-artifacts`, `~/mc/brief/ios-build`, `~/mc/proposals/archive`, `~/mc/intake/decisions-archive`: each has its own owner and its own question.
Rotating `runs.tsv` or `gate-rounds.jsonl`: the daily gates, the closable check and the gate history read them whole, and both are small (300 KB, 32 MB on 2026-10-11).
Retention for `mc brief` and `mc helper` transcripts: they keep today's `mc work tidy` rule (14 days, the newest kept).
Removing the legacy fallback for areas directly under `~/mc/<project>/`. That is a later one-line change, once none remain.
Worktrees of `~/memoro` registered outside `~/mc`, under `/private/tmp/claude-*` and `memoro/.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. Tidy lists them and does not remove them.
A per-step cost attribution beyond what `runs.tsv` rows carry: a session belongs to a step through its `pr` column or not at all.

steps.title: 3. The closeout: written by the archive, in git
steps.done_when: The archive commit for a done project also adds `docs/project/<programme>/closeout/<project>.json`. Archived projects that still have a register file and no closeout get one in the next archive PR, at most 40 per PR. `npm test` is green.
instruction: New pure module `src/mc/closeout.js`: `buildCloseout({ plan, entry, runs, sessions, archivedAt })` → object, plus `closeoutPath(programme, project)` → `docs/project/<programme>/closeout/<project>.json`. Shape: `{ schema: 'mc-closeout', version: 1, project, programme, repo, plan_path, archived: <yyyy-mm-dd>, goal: plan.goal, success_criteria: plan.success_criteria, steps: [...], sessions: [...], totals: {...} }`.

`steps[i]`: `{ title, done_when }` from the plan, plus from the register entry (`readEntry`, `src/mc/register.js:359`): `status, pr, landed: { sha, into, at } | null, attempts, reason, comments`, and `sessions` / `seconds` / `cost_usd` summed over the session rows whose `pr` equals the step's `pr`.

`sessions`: every `runs.tsv` row with `name === project` and kind other than `merge`/`mend`, in order, as `{ ts, kind, seconds, land_seconds, pr, turns, input, output, cache_read, cache_write, model, note, session, cost_usd }`. `RUNS_HEADER` is at `src/mc/run-plan.js:35`; parse with `parseRuns` (`brief-collect.js:216`). runs.tsv has **no cost column**: `cost_usd` is `total_cost_usd` from the session's result json, matched by `session_id` across `sessions` (a list of parsed result objects the caller reads), else `null`. Never estimate it.

`totals`: `{ sessions, seconds, land_seconds, cost_usd (sum of known, plus 'cost_unknown': count of nulls), input, output, cache_read, cache_write, first: first ts, landed: last landed.at }`. Write the file with `JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2) + '\n'`.

Reading the session results is the caller's job (`run.js`, via `deps`): for each runs.tsv session id, look under `paths.log` for `<project>-<stamp>.json` and `<project>-<stamp>.json.gz`, using the exact name match `^<project>-\d{8}T\d{6}Z\.json(\.gz)?$`. A plain prefix would make `ui-faults` read `ui-faults-2`'s files. Gunzip with `node:zlib` `gunzipSync`. Since 2026-10-10 about 1,300 of them are gzipped. A file that does not parse is skipped.

`archiveIn` (`src/mc/run.js` ~1299): for each plan it archives, before the commit, build the closeout from the plan text it already read, the register entry, runs.tsv and the session results, and write it into the archive worktree at `closeoutPath`. Then `git add` it. It is part of the same commit and PR (`Archive N done project(s)…`, ~1355). The PR body gets one line: `Each project's closeout is in docs/project/<programme>/closeout/.` A closeout that fails to build is skipped for that project, the archive goes on, and a say line names the project and the reason. Step 4 then never purges that project, because the closeout is missing.

Backfill in the same chore: `archiveDone` (~1245) also takes archived projects (`archivedProjects`, ~1548, rows in `project_log.md`) in this repo, whose register file exists, whose closeout path is absent on `origin/main`, and whose plan directory is absent on `origin/main`. It takes at most `CLOSEOUT_BACKFILL_MAX = 40` per PR (an exported constant whose comment says why: one reviewable PR). It takes the plan text from git history: `git log -1 --format=%H --diff-filter=D origin/main -- <register.plan>`, then `git show <sha>^:<register.plan>`. When that fails, `goal`/`success_criteria`/titles are `null` and the file says `plan: null`. The register's `plan` field gives the path, and its `repo` field says which repository's archive takes it. When the batch holds only backfills, the PR title is `Closeout N archived project(s): a, b, …`, it lands the same way (`landDocsPr`), and it waits behind an open `mc-archive-*` PR like any archive.

`docs/project/README.md`: one paragraph under *Who writes what* says `closeout/` under a programme is the archive's, holds one JSON per archived project, is never a project name, and that nothing reads it but people. `docs/technical/mc-tidy.md` gets a section `## The closeout` stating what it holds and when it is written.

Tests: `tests/mc/closeout.test.js` covers a fixture with two steps. Step 1 has two sessions (one `.json`, one `.json.gz`), step 2 has one session with no result file. Expect: per-step sums, `cost_unknown: 1`, `ui-faults` not reading `ui-faults-2-…` files, and the exact JSON text of a small case. `tests/mc/archive-live.test.js`: the archive commit contains `docs/project//closeout/

.json` and the `git rm`. A backfill case: a project in `project_log.md`, register present, plan deleted in history, gives one closeout file with the plan's goal from history and a `Closeout 1 archived project` title. `tests/architecture/plan-file-shape.test.js` stays green (a `closeout/` directory has no PLAN.json and is skipped). `npm test` green.

steps.title: 4. `mc tidy`: list first, then remove, per root; the runner runs it
steps.done_when: `mc tidy [--apply] [--json]` writes `~/mc/runner/tidy/<stamp>.json` with every target and every keep and the rule for each, and with `--apply` removes only that file's targets after re-checking each. `mc work tidy` is the same command. The runner runs it daily (`TIDY_KIND`) and at most hourly while a lane skips for disk, `runner.log` rotates at 32 MiB, and `npm test` is green.
instruction: Build on `src/mc/work-tidy.js` and keep its shape: `gatherTidyFacts` → pure `tidyPlan` → `applyTidy`. Rename the module `src/mc/tidy.js`. `src/mc/work-tidy.js` re-exports it, and `mc work tidy` (`commands/work.js:265–309`) calls the same entry. New top-level verb `mc tidy` in `src/mc/commands/tidy.js`, registered in `src/mc-verbs.js` beside `work` (:12), with `--apply`, `--json`, and `--days <n>` (kept for the brief/helper rule). Add it to `help-text.js`.

The list file: `gatherTidyFacts` + `tidyPlan` produce `{ at, rules_version: 1, targets: [{ path, kind, rule, why, bytes }], kept: [{ path, rule, why }] }`. Before any removal, and on dry runs too, it is written with `writeJsonAtomic` (`src/mc/atomic-write.js`) to `~/mc/runner/tidy/<stamp>.json`. Keep the newest 30 list files and remove older ones in the same apply. `applyTidy({ listPath })` reads that file back and acts only on its `targets`. For each target it: (a) asserts `realpath` is under the allowed root for its `kind` (contract), (b) re-runs that target's rule on fresh facts, and (c) removes with `rmSync({ recursive: true })` or `git worktree remove` (no `--force`) + `branch -D` through `releaseWorkArea`. If any of these throws or answers no, the target is kept and the reason recorded. The apply's result is appended to the same list file as `applied: [{ path, ok, why }]`.

Rules, one function each, each returning `{ target: bool, why }`, and any exception is `{ target: false, why: 'error: …' }`. (P) Project purge: for each register file `~/mc/runner/projects/

.json` whose project meets the contract's four conditions, the targets are the register file, `~/mc/runner/log/

-.{jsonl,json,json.err}[.gz]` (exact-name regex as in step 3), `~/mc/runner/log/closed/

/`, `~/mc/runner/scratch/

-/`, and every `~/.claude/projects/

/.jsonl` (+ `/`) whose head `cwd` (`readHead`, `src/mc/conversations.js:209`) is under `/step/

/` or legacy `/

/`. Ask `origin/main` with one `git ls-tree` per repo, and read `project_log.md` with `git show origin/main:docs/project/project_log.md`. A git that cannot answer means no purge this run. (G) Programme transcripts: for each `~/.claude/projects/

` whose transcripts' head `cwd` is a planning area `/plan/` or below, keep the newest by mtime, keep every one modified within `PROGRAMME_TRANSCRIPT_KEEP_MS = 72 h` (exported, with a comment quoting Martin, 2026-10-11: "alltid behålla den aktuella; gamla kan städas efter 72h"), and target the rest. `memory/` is never read or listed. (X) Extra plan worktrees: under each `/plan//`, every direct child with `.git` other than `memoro` and `memoro-cli` is a target when `releaseVerdict` (`work-area.js:369`) says `worktree and branch`. Its `processesStandingIn` (`src/mc/standing.js:70`, one `cwdsOfUser` lsof per run) must be empty, and an lsof that fails keeps everything. (W) Work areas: never targets. Listed under `kept` with rule `work-area`. (S) Step areas: never targets here. `closeWorkareas` closes them. (L) Existing `mc work tidy` transcript and leftover rules (T1–T5, `work-tidy.js:281–307`) apply unchanged to transcripts that P and G do not claim, with step areas counted as areas. (R) Foreign worktrees: `git worktree list --porcelain` of `~/memoro` and `~/memoro-cli` entries outside `` are listed under `kept` with rule `foreign-worktree`. Then `git worktree prune` runs on both repos.

Output: the dry run prints per rule a count and the summed `bytes` (size from `lstat`, walking directories in node), the first 10 targets, every keep whose why is not routine, and `list: ~/mc/runner/tidy/<stamp>.json`. `--apply` prints `freed <n> GB in <m> items, kept <k> on re-check` and logs `tidy` to `mc.log`. `--json` prints the list object.

Runner, `chores()` (`src/mc/run.js:2833`): after `sweepScratch`, `runTidyDaily()` modelled on `runDepsDaily` (~1679–1705). `TIDY_KIND = 'tidy'` lives in `run-plan.js` beside `DEPS_KIND` (:568), and `nightlyDue({ kind: TIDY_KIND })` is the cadence. It calls the tidy entry with apply, writes a `logRun` row of kind `tidy` whose note is `freed=<bytes>,items=<n>,kept=<k>`, and says one line. Disk: when `diskRoom` (~2786) has made a lane return `skipped:disk`, the next chore pass runs tidy too, at most once per `TIDY_DISK_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 1 h`, tracked in memory. The archive and close chores run before it in the same pass, so a project archived this pass is purged by the next.

`runner.log`: `say()` (`run.js:610–614`) rotates the file to `runner.log.1` when it is over `RUNNER_LOG_MAX_BYTES = 32 MiB`, checked once per chore pass, not per line. Make `rotateIfLarge` in `src/mc/logger.js:170` an export taking `(path, maxBytes)` and use it, keeping one generation. `scripts/measure-steps.py:17` reads `runner.log` and also reads `runner.log.1` when it exists.

Docs: `docs/technical/mc-tidy.md` gets `## mc tidy`, with the roots table (plan / step / work / state), each rule P, G, X, W, S, L, R in one paragraph, the list file, the daily and disk triggers, and what is never touched (the contract's list). Ruling 39 is linked from it.

Tests: `tests/mc/tidy.test.js` (move and extend `tests/mc/work-tidy.test.js`) works over a temp home and a temp `~/.claude/projects` with git faked as in the existing file. The fixture has: an archived project with closeout and no area (all of P's targets, `ui-faults` vs `ui-faults-2` names), an archived project without closeout (nothing), an archived project whose legacy area still exists (nothing), and a project with a step blocked on a time (nothing). For a programme it has 4 transcripts (newest 5 days old: kept; one 10 h old: kept; two 4 days old: targets) and a `memory/` directory, which is never listed. It also has a plan area with `memoro`, `memoro-cli`, a merged clean `wt-a` (target), a dirty `wt-b` (kept), a merged `wt-c` with a process in it (kept), a `work/x` area (kept, `work-area`), and an lsof that throws (X keeps all). Apply cases: a target whose rule flips between list and apply is kept; a path outside the roots in a hand-edited list is refused; the list file is written before the first `rmSync` (spy order). In `tests/mc/run.test.js`: tidy runs once per 24 h by `TIDY_KIND` row and once after a `skipped:disk` within the hour limit, and `runner.log` rotates over the limit. `npm test` green.
